samples.claim: Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407).
samples.evidence:
410 | /* Fixed width items placed contiguously in a single buffer
411 |  *
412 |  * This is a leaf encoding, there is no compression applied to the data.
413 |  *
414 |  * This is a transparent encoding by definition.
415 |  *
416 |  * The input is a fixed-width data block.
417 |  * The output is a single buffer.
418 |  */
419 | message Flat {
420 |   /* the number of bits per value, must be greater than 0, does
421 |    * not need to be a multiple of 8
422 |    */
423 |   uint64 bits_per_value = 1;
424 |   // The compression applied to the data
425 |   optional BufferCompression data = 2;
426 | }
427 |

429 |  * offsets are output as a data block that may be further compressed.
430 |  *

433 |  *
434 |  * This is a transparent encoding by definition.
435 |  *

437 |  * The output is a single fixed-width data block (the offsets) and

439 |  */

answers.write_then_compact: FAIL. KB explains schema import, manifest sharing/detachment, deletion predicates, ordered remapping, local row-ID construction/serialization and cursor costs. Segment construction collects a Vec and may scan the whole numeric span; sequence serialization clones and collects protobuf segments (segment.rs126-299; serde.rs232-344). Dataset::write/compact entry points, file IO scheduling, actual allocation ownership through compaction, index remapping lifecycle, atomic commit and cleanup remain missing. Local arithmetic is insufficient for complete disk/memory trace.
answers.new_scalar_index: FAIL. KB supplies schema-message/package constraints, IndexMetadata coverage and cache codec, overlay stale sets and core Bloom behavior. Cookbook explicitly lacks index traits, registration/loader dispatch, planner, write/update integration, tests and binding mappings. It cannot provide a complete implementable scalar-index recipe.
answers.v2_format: FAIL. KB specifies schema envelope order and derived40-byte footer, selectors Stable2.2/Next2.3, exact identity mappings and eight-byte footer recognition (file2.proto11-115; version.rs19-262; lib.rs25-60). It records schema gates for2.2 large chunks/constants/packed structs and2.3 sparse layout, plus implemented table feature flags. Full encoder/reader algorithms, exhaustive runtime gates, historical fixtures and list-null equality discrepancy remain unresolved. Two stale pending-status statements were additionally found in cross-layer review.
answers.python_api: FAIL. Python/PyO3 APIs have not been analyzed. Contributor environment policy and core Rust APIs provide no complete Python signatures, defaults, exceptions or Rust binding mapping.
answers.transaction_commit: FAIL. KB supplies protobuf operations, schema-change classifier, key filter representation, local manifest/lineage transformations, capability flags and typed unknown-commit/conflict errors. Runtime operation enum, operation-pair conflict matrix, manifest-builder orchestration, retries, atomic object-store publication and full new-operation recipe remain missing.
